description_good.justification: The README at https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity#readme opens by stating what the software does and the problem it addresses.

interact.justification: Issues and pull requests are open on GitHub; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md states how to propose changes and report problems.

contribution.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md states how a change is proposed and what it must pass.

contribution_requirements.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements a change must meet.

documentation_basics.justification: The repository's documentation covers installation and use, and renders as a site at https://manifest-identity.github.io/manifest-identity/.

documentation_interface.justification: The interface is documented in the repository, the documentation is checked against the running interface, and the application serves interactive interface documentation.

repo_track.justification: Every change is tracked in version control and reaches the default branch through a pull request.

repo_interim.justification: Every interim change lands as a pull request on the public repository; nothing is batched into releases.

version_unique.justification: One tag per release, in semantic versioning form; the release process is recorded in the repository's decisions.

version_semver.justification: Semantic versioning. The current release is the newest tag on the repository's releases page.

version_tags.justification: Every release is a signed tag; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/tags

release_notes.justification: Each release at https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/releases carries notes, and the repository's roadmap states what comes next.

release_notes_vulns.justification: SECURITY.md commits to naming every fixed vulnerability in the release notes.

report_responses.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/SECURITY.md states how quickly reports are acknowledged and answered.

enhancement_responses.justification: Enhancement requests are answered in the issue tracker on the same commitments.

vulnerability_report_process.justification: https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/blob/main/SECURITY.md: private reporting through GitHub security advisories.

build.justification: The repository documents one way to build and run the software from a fresh clone, with dependencies fixed to exact, verified versions.

build_common_tools.justification: Common, free tools only; the repository documents the build.

test.justification: An automated test suite runs in continuous integration on every change, and a pull request cannot merge until it passes.

test_invocation.justification: One documented command runs the whole suite; the repository states it.

test_most.justification: Coverage is held above a floor enforced in continuous integration, and controls are proven by removing each one and requiring the tests to notice.

test_policy.justification: The repository's contributing rules require tests with new functionality, and continuous integration enforces a coverage floor on every change.

tests_are_added.justification: Every functional change in the history lands with its tests, and continuous integration enforces a coverage floor on every change.

warnings.justification: Linting and strict typing run in continuous integration.

warnings_fixed.justification: The pipeline is clean of warnings; a new warning fails the build.

warnings_strict.justification: The strictest settings of the linter and the type checker are on.

know_secure_design.justification: The repository documents how each request is protected and what the software defends against, and carries a threat model.

know_common_errors.justification: Input handling is documented and tested: escaping at every exit, formula-safe exports, text-only rendering, parameterized queries.

crypto_published.justification: Only published algorithms, through libraries; transport security belongs to the deployment platform.

crypto_call.justification: Cryptography is used only through established libraries and the language's standard library; nothing is implemented in the project.

crypto_floss.justification: The libraries used are free and open source software.

crypto_keylength.justification: Library defaults for a published, memory-hard password hash; tokens from the standard library's secure random source at its recommended size.

crypto_working.justification: No broken cryptographic algorithm is used for any security purpose.

crypto_pfs.justification: The application terminates no TLS itself; transport security is the deployment platform's.

crypto_password_storage.justification: Passwords are stored only as salted hashes from a published, memory-hard algorithm, through a library.

crypto_random.justification: Every token comes from the standard library's cryptographically secure random source.

delivery_mitm.justification: Delivery over HTTPS; releases are signed and carry verifiable provenance.

delivery_unsigned.justification: Every release asset carries build provenance that a consumer can verify against the platform's log; https://github.com/manifest-identity/manifest-identity/releases

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: None outstanding; dependency advisories are received and reviewed as they arrive.

static_analysis.justification: Static analysis, including security queries, runs on every change and on a schedule, with strict typing and linting; the repository names the analyzers.

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: Security-focused static analysis runs over the code and the pipeline definitions; the repository names the analyzers.

dynamic_analysis.justification: The parsers that read outside input are fuzzed under a memory-error detector on changes and on a schedule, beside property-based tests in the suite.

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: Assertions are active in every test run.

test_continuous_integration.justification: Continuous integration runs on every push and pull request, and its checks must pass before a merge to the default branch.

no_leaked_credentials.justification: The full history is scanned for credentials at every commit and in continuous integration, with findings verified against their providers.

english.justification: All documentation and discussion are in English.

maintained.justification: Actively developed. Every change reaches the default branch through a reviewed pull request with required checks, releases are cut from the maintainer's signed tag and listed on the repository's releases page, and the roadmap in the repository states what comes next.
